summary: New Hampshire has no sales tax, but meals are taxed at 8.5% by its Meals and Rooms Tax (RSA 78-A), which this rate is.

citations.title: NH DRA: Meals & Rooms (Rentals) Tax
citations.quote: The tax rate is 8.5% for taxable periods beginning October 1, 2021.

notes: The Meals and Rooms Tax is a separate state tax, not in OpenTaxRate's general rates (which are 0 in NH); this rule's rate is that tax. Before 2021-10-01 the rate was 9%: not researched. Added 2026-10-30 for an exception a development benchmark case exposed; cites the agency page that case quotes.

summary: New Hampshire's 8.5% meals tax doesn't reach bakery products sold in units of 6 or more, or food products provided by a store; bakery items a restaurant sells singly are taxable meals.

conditions.when: Sold by a restaurant in units of fewer than 6, ready to eat
Sold in units of 6 or more

citations.title: RSA 78-A:3, Definitions (VIII, "Meal")
citations.quote: The term shall not include food products provided by a store or bakery products when sold in units of 6 or more.

citations.title: NH DRA, Meals and Rooms (Rentals) Tax
citations.quote: The tax rate is 8.5% for taxable periods beginning October 1, 2021.

notes: Added 2026-10-30 after held-out case ho-nh-04 showed the inherited food.prepared rule taxed a box of six doughnuts; RSA 78-A:3 is that case's source, so ho-nh-04 no longer counts as held out. Dated from the 8.5% rate.

summary: New Hampshire's meals tax doesn't reach food products a store provides: a grocery deli's coleslaw or potato salad, in any quantity, isn't a taxable meal unless sold as part of a combination plate.

conditions.when: deli items sold by the container or weight
sold as part of a combination plate

citations.title: RSA 78-A:3, Definitions (VIII, "Meal")
citations.quote: The term shall not include food products provided by a store or bakery products when sold in units of 6 or more.

citations.title: NH DRA TIR 2007-005
citations.quote: Deli items, such as coleslaw, potato salad, etc, in any quantity, unless sold as part of a combination plate.

citations.title: NH DRA Meals and Rooms Tax FAQ
citations.quote: Effective October 1, 2021 the Meals and Rentals Tax rate is 8.5%.

notes: Added 2026-11-01 after dev case d2-nh-02 showed the inherited food.prepared rule taxed a grocery deli's sides. Dated from the 8.5% rate.

summary: New Hampshire has no sales tax, and food a seller assembled for the buyer to cook is not a 'meal' under its Meals and Rooms Tax, which reaches only food available for immediate consumption without further significant preparation.

citations.title: RSA 78-A:3, Definitions (VIII, "Meal")
citations.quote: provided by a restaurant in such form as to be available for immediate consumption without further significant preparation

citations.title: NH DRA, General Information FAQ
citations.quote: No, there is no general sales tax on goods purchased in New Hampshire.

notes: No NH source read (RSA 78-A:3, Rev 700 as readopted 2024-10-29) names take-and-bake pizza, raw kebabs or meal kits; the rule reads baking or cooking as 'further significant preparation'. Earliest date: 2021-10-01, as for the NH food.prepared rule; the RSA text read is the current one, and earlier text was not compared. NH has no local sales taxes.
